findings.summary: Seven recurring patterns drawn across the wider investigation. (1) A regulatory revolving door around crypto-custody firms appears in four instances: a three-instance Skadden-or-equivalent to OCC to implementation pipeline (Brooks 2020 Coinbase to OCC to Bitfury; Gould 2025 Bitfury/BlackRock/Promontory to OCC; Cohen 2025 Skadden to OCC to Erebor approval, with Cohen's 65-day window the tightest), plus a parallel custody-firm to OMB to Schaerr Jaffe to OMB route via Paoletta (2018 and 2025) at OMB, CFPB, and OIRA, structurally distinct from the OCC pipeline. (2) Brooks-era Interpretive Letters #1170/#1174 and #1184 remain operative law cited in the Erebor approval letter, so the earlier deregulation framework now underpins WLFI/Tahnoon flows. (3) Aryam Investment 1, a Tahnoon vehicle, bought 49% of WLFI for $500M ($187M to Trump-family entities); G42's Edelman and Xiao were seated without disclosure; MGX deployed $2B in WLFI USD1 to Binance in May 2025. (4) The Mubadala-as-recurring-sponsor model maps onto three SCFEA sovereign pillars (ADIA, Mubadala, and L'IMAD, roughly $300B after the January 2026 consolidation under Khaled bin Mohamed bin Zayed), a regulatory layer (Al Shorafa across ADX, SCA, and ADGM Vice Chair), and a US-listing layer (Kazim as Nasdaq Inc. director via Borse Dubai), with the bridging roles outlasting individual principals. (5) Several trades cluster ahead of the January 2025 Stargate window: a Bitfury $53.9M dividend on Dec 23 2024 (38 days before the Cipher PIPE), AltC's May 2024 close with an unusual $7,457.80 redemption out of roughly 30M shares (PIPE backstop not triggered), Crusoe's start of Abilene construction in June 2024 (seven months before the Stargate announcement), and SoftBank's full exit from Cipher in Q3 2025, suggesting Stargate largely re-bundled infrastructure already in motion. (6) The Klein-Altman-Oklo and Stargate-MGX threads are separate at the SEC primary-source level despite press treatment merging them; Altman resigned the Oklo board on Apr 22 2025, three months after the Stargate announcement. (7) bin Sulayem resigned from DP World on Feb 13 2026 after the DOJ Epstein release, the first observed setback for the Tahnoon network on Epstein-related exposure, with replacement Kazim maintaining US-market access via a Nasdaq Inc. board seat. Additional record corrections: Stéphane resolves to Bertrand G. des Pallières; Antoine Bremner (unverified) is likely Christopher Bremner; Compagnie Du Saleve B223232 was incorporated in 2018 and so cannot be the 28 Oct 2015 entity (likely the closed French SARL #803012046 instead); SKAS is the Saker Aviation Services ticker rather than a partners' acronym; the Hoffenberg 'Gold shielded Epstein' claim has no docket support in 1:94-cr-00213.

curation.lead:
Khaldoon Khalifa Al Mubarak (born 1976, Abu Dhabi) is the Managing Director and Group CEO of Mubadala Investment Company, the Abu Dhabi sovereign wealth vehicle reporting roughly $330 billion in assets under management, and according to Mubadala's 2025 disclosures and Gulf Business reporting holds concurrent senior board positions across the principal Abu Dhabi state-capital and AI institutions: Chairman of Abu Dhabi Commercial Bank, Vice Chairman of MGX, board director of ADNOC, G42, Aldar Properties, First Abu Dhabi Bank, and Emirates Foundation, Chairman of the Executive Affairs Authority, board director of L'IMAD Holding following the January 2026 Supreme Council for Financial and Economic Affairs (SCFEA) consolidation, Chair of the Mohamed bin Zayed University of Artificial Intelligence Board of Trustees from February 2025, and Secretary General of the Artificial Intelligence and Advanced Technology Council from October 2025 [Finding #11203].

Analysis of the documented record positions Al Mubarak as an operational bridge across a three-pillar structure of Abu Dhabi sovereign capital: ADIA, Mubadala, and L'IMAD Holding (the consolidated approximately $300 billion vehicle under Khaled bin Mohamed bin Zayed following the January 2026 SCFEA resolution), alongside a regulatory layer through Mohamed Ali Al Shorafa across ADX, SCA, and ADGM, and a US-listing layer through Essa Kazim's Borse Dubai-Nasdaq board seat [Finding #11236]. Within that architecture, Al Mubarak runs the Mubadala pillar while sitting as Vice Chairman under Sheikh Tahnoon bin Zayed Al Nahyan at MGX Fund Management Limited (formed March 12, 2024 with a $100 billion AUM target) and as a director under Tahnoon at G42 and First Abu Dhabi Bank [Finding #11220][Finding #4262].

Al Mubarak's Mubadala mandate includes a multi-year partnership with Apollo Global Management, extended on November 11, 2024 with a $2.5 billion joint venture to co-invest in global private credit, anchor positions in the Middle Market Apollo Institutional Private Lending vehicle launched in 2024, and an Apollo investment into Mubadala Capital Solutions [Finding #11196]. Cross-references in the Epstein corpus place Al Mubarak inside the Abu Dhabi sovereign structure as early as October 2017, when an EFTA02586299 email from David Stern to Jeffrey Epstein recorded that Sheikh Mohammed bin Zayed had delegated digital-currency policy to Al Mubarak at Mubadala [Finding #3745]. Records indicate Al Mubarak's role is that of a career executive providing structural bridging across the sovereign-capital pillars rather than direct deal sponsorship [Finding #11236]
curation.system_role: Al Mubarak occupies an operational bridge position within Abu Dhabi's sovereign-capital structure. He runs the Mubadala pillar in his own right while sitting on the boards of every Tahnoon-chaired commercial vehicle (MGX, G42, FAB), giving him simultaneous authority across what would otherwise be parallel sovereign portfolios. On the available record, this dual-pillar role is the structural mechanism by which Mubadala-sponsored capital and Tahnoon-cluster MGX/G42 capital reach the same downstream deployment surfaces — including US private credit (Apollo), AI infrastructure (the MGX-Microsoft-BlackRock-GIP partnership and Stargate), and crypto and Trump-affiliated transactions — through a coordinated rather than competitive allocation pattern.

sections.title: Career and Institutional Roles
sections.content:
Mubadala's 2025 official biography, Wikipedia, and Gulf Business reporting on Al Mubarak's directorship slate set out concurrent 2025 institutional roles spanning much of the Abu Dhabi sovereign-commercial structure: Managing Director and Group CEO of Mubadala Investment Company at approximately $330 billion AUM; Chairman of Abu Dhabi Commercial Bank; Vice Chairman of MGX (under Tahnoon as Chairman); board member of ADNOC, G42, Aldar Properties, First Abu Dhabi Bank, and Emirates Foundation; Chair of the MBZUAI Board of Trustees from February 2025; Secretary General of the Artificial Intelligence and Advanced Technology Council from October 2025 (under Tahnoon as Chairman); Chairman of the Executive Affairs Authority of the Abu Dhabi government; and a director of L'IMAD Holding following the January 2026 SCFEA consolidation [Finding #11203].

The composition is unusual in scale even by Gulf sovereign standards. Al Mubarak holds simultaneous chairmanships at a major commercial bank (ADCB), a sovereign wealth fund (Mubadala), an executive government body (Executive Affairs Authority), and the country's flagship AI university (MBZUAI), while also sitting on the boards of two Tahnoon-chaired vehicles (MGX and FAB) and the country's primary AI champion (G42, also Tahnoon-chaired) [Finding #11203]. The roles concentrate decision-making authority across banking, sovereign asset allocation, AI policy, and government affairs in a single executive [Finding #11203].

Corporate registry materials and reporting on Manchester City Football Club record that Al Mubarak has chaired the City Football Group since the 2008 Abu Dhabi acquisition of the Premier League club, sitting alongside non-executive director Martin Edelman, who participated in facilitating the acquisition [Finding #4033]. The Manchester City board overlaps with the MBZUAI Board of Trustees on which both also serve, providing a long-running board-level interlock independent of the Mubadala-MGX corporate structure [Finding #4033]

sections.title: Mubadala Leadership and the Apollo Partnership
sections.content:
Under Al Mubarak's leadership, Mubadala operates as the Abu Dhabi sovereign portfolio for diversified international investment; analysis of the sovereign structure distinguishes it from ADIA's foreign-reserves mandate and from L'IMAD's January 2026 consolidated vehicle for ADQ-adjacent commercial holdings [Finding #11203][Finding #11236]. A November 11, 2024 announcement set out an extended multi-year partnership between Mubadala and Apollo Global Management with quantified scope: a $2.5 billion joint venture to co-invest in global private credit; a Mubadala anchor position in Apollo's 2024 Middle Market Apollo Institutional Private Lending platform; an Apollo investment into Mubadala Capital Solutions launched in 2023; and a continuation of Mubadala's anchor commitment to Apollo Strategic Origination Partners established in 2020 [Finding #11196]. The named counterparties were Jim Zelter (Apollo Co-President, Asset Management) and Omar Eraiqat (Mubadala Deputy CEO, Diversified Investments) [Finding #11196].

Mubadala separately disclosed in its 2024 annual report a roughly $20 billion private-credit portfolio spread across Apollo, Ares, Carlyle, Goldman Sachs, and KKR, which places the Apollo extension as the largest of several parallel relationships rather than an exclusive arrangement [Finding #11196]. Earlier claims of a 49% Mubadala stake in Apollo are not supported by primary disclosures and have been retracted; the verified structure is a joint-venture-plus-anchor-LP arrangement across multiple Apollo origination platforms [Finding #11196].

The Mubadala-Apollo channel is the single largest documented mechanism by which Abu Dhabi sovereign capital reaches US private credit markets [Finding #11196]. Separately, ADQ — the Abu Dhabi Developmental Holding Company — filed a Schedule 13D in September-October 2023 reporting beneficial ownership in Vista Credit Strategic Lending Corp through subsidiary Sapphire Private Funds Holdings II RSC Ltd, with named filer Khalifa Alsuwaidi, one of multiple parallel UAE sovereign positions in US private-credit vehicles [Finding #11200].

sections.title: Bridge Position Across the Tahnoon-Aligned Cluster
sections.content:
Al Mubarak runs Mubadala — a vehicle that is not under Tahnoon's direct chairmanship — while his board inventory reaches into every major Tahnoon-aligned institution [Finding #11203]. On the ADGM register and the company website, the MGX board comprises Tahnoon as Chairman, Al Mubarak as Vice Chairman, Jassem Al Zaabi (Abu Dhabi Department of Finance Chairman and AI Council Secretary General), Peng Xiao (G42 CEO), Martin Edelman (G42 General Counsel), and Ahmed Yahia Al Idrissi (MD/CEO) [Finding #4006]. G42's 2025 board roster lists a seven-member board with Tahnoon as Chairman alongside Al Mubarak, Al Zaabi, Brad Smith (Microsoft President), Egon Durban (Silver Lake Co-CEO), Peng Xiao, and Martin Edelman as directors [Finding #4262].

This configuration, on cross-reference of the MGX, G42, and FAB rosters, places Al Mubarak as an operational bridge in the three-pillar model — the Mubadala pillar he runs directly, plus the ADIA and L'IMAD pillars chaired by other principals, with a regulatory layer through Mohamed Ali Al Shorafa across ADX, SCA, and ADGM, and a US-listing layer through Essa Kazim's Borse Dubai-Nasdaq board seat [Finding #11236]. Analysis of the same record suggests that the operational consequence of his dual-pillar position is that Mubadala-sponsored deal flow and Tahnoon-cluster MGX/G42 deal flow reach the same downstream surfaces in a coordinated allocation pattern rather than as independent commercial decisions [Finding #11236].

MGX was formed on March 12, 2024 by Mubadala and G42 as founding partners, operating under the AI and Advanced Technology Council established January 22, 2024 by Sheikh Mohamed bin Zayed, with three investment pillars (AI infrastructure, semiconductors, and AI core technology) and a $100 billion AUM target [Finding #11220]. On cross-reference of the MGX documentation and the ADGM register, its ownership chain runs G42 Holding (75%+) → GX Investments (50–75%) → MGX Group Holding 1 LTD, with Tahnoon as Chair, Al Mubarak as Vice Chair, and Ahmed Yahia Al Idrissi as CEO [Finding #4062]. Subsequent MGX activity reported by CNBC in October 2025 includes the September 2024 Global AI Infrastructure Investment Partnership with BlackRock and Microsoft, the January 2025 Stargate joint venture, and reported stakes in xAI, Anthropic, OpenAI (via secondaries), Reka, plus Trump-affiliated crypto and TikTok positions [Finding #11220].

Al Mubarak's October 2025 appointment as Secretary General of the Artificial Intelligence and Advanced Technology Council places him directly under Tahnoon (the Council's Chairman) in an explicitly state-aligned policy role coordinating UAE AI strategy, layered atop his existing executive position at Mubadala and his MBZUAI Board of Trustees chairmanship from February 2025 [Finding #11203]. Read together, his AIATC, MBZUAI, MGX, and Mubadala roles concentrate AI-policy, AI-academic, and AI-capital-allocation authority under coordinated UAE-state direction [Finding #11203]

sections.title: Historical Context: Epstein-Era Abu Dhabi Channels
sections.content:
An email logged as EFTA02586299, dated October 5, 2017, records David Stern writing to Jeffrey Epstein on two contemporaneous items: that Sheikh Mohammed bin Zayed had delegated digital-currency matters to Al Mubarak at Mubadala, and that Stern was attempting to broker a meeting between Leon Black and Ahmed Ali Al Sayegh (the Abu Dhabi Global Market chairman, described as "very close to the boss") [Finding #3745]. Records show that the Abu Dhabi sovereign structure Epstein was attempting to access in 2017 is the same institutional set — Mubadala, ADGM, MBZ-family principals — through which Al Mubarak now operates as Mubadala MD/CEO and as a director of every Tahnoon-aligned vehicle [Finding #3863].

Examination of the Epstein corpus shows that the documented Epstein-era Abu Dhabi channels included Ian Osborne (a Mubadala board member who coordinated tech investments with Epstein in 2012); David Stern (who continued Mubadala meetings through December 2018); and Martin Edelman (referenced on a December 2016 Epstein calendar entry and on an Epstein "list for bannon steve" — Edelman now signs World Liberty Financial's Aryam-WLFI agreement as a G42 designee), through the same institutions that now channel capital into Trump-family ventures via MGX, WLFI, and the USD1 stablecoin [Finding #4102][Finding #3863]. Analysis of the records indicates institutional continuity rather than a new relationship: the Abu Dhabi sovereign structure that interfaced with Epstein in 2012-2018 is the same structure through which Al Mubarak now bridges Mubadala and Tahnoon-cluster vehicles [Finding #4102].

A New Yorker profile of Ari Emanuel records that Martin Edelman introduced Emanuel to Al Mubarak as part of facilitating Sheikh Tahnoon's roughly $200 million handshake investment for 10% of UFC with Lorenzo Fertitta a year later, an indication of Al Mubarak's role as a long-standing relay point between Western corporate principals and the MBZ family well before the post-2024 MGX-WLFI cycle [Finding #4033]. The same Edelman-Al Mubarak relationship runs through both the Manchester City and MBZUAI boards on which they sit, providing continuous board-level contact independent of the Mubadala-MGX corporate structure [Finding #4033]

Martin Edelman.target: Sheikh Tahnoon bin Zayed Al Nahyan
Martin Edelman.description: Edelman is GC of G42 (Tahnoon's AI company), MGX board member, Mubadala adviser. Led China divestiture negotiations with US government alongside Tahnoon.

Edelman met MBZ during 2002 Gulf tour with Gen Tommy Franks. Became senior adviser to Mubadala the Abu Dhabi sovereign fund. Appointed Mubadala designee on AMD board 2013 and GlobalFoundries board 2017. Reportedly granted Emirati citizenship.
Co-signatories on Aryam-WLFI agreement. Both placed on WLFI board without public disclosure. Peng Xiao is G42 CEO where Edelman is General Counsel.

Gen Franks was CENTCOM commander for Afghanistan and Iraq. Edelman accompanied Franks on Gulf tours in 2002 where he first met MBZ and Tahnoon. Franks visited Arab leaders monthly. Edelman received Dept of Army Public Service Award 2007.
Edelman sits on WLFI 5-person board as Aryam/G42 appointee. Not listed on WLFI website team page despite board seat.

Sheikh Tahnoon bin Zayed Al Nahyan.description: Witkoff is Trump Middle East envoy negotiating with UAE officials including Tahnoon while Witkoff family profits from Tahnoon's M WLFI investment. Son Zach is WLFI co-founder.
UAE entity Aryam Investment 1 acquired 49% WLFI stake for M; controlled by Tahnoon who is UAE national security adviser
Tahnoon-backed Aryam Investment 1 acquired 49% of WLFI for USD500M. Tahnoon controls all entities involved (G42, Aryam, MGX).

Tahnoon chairs MGX which holds 15% of TikTok USDS JV. Separately, Tahnoon's IHC/Lunate subsidiary inherited ByteDance stake from G42's 42XFund. Dual economic interest on both sides of the TikTok divestiture.

Through Aryam Investment 1, acquired 49% stake in WLF for $500M (Jan 2025, pre-inauguration). G42 executives got board seats. Tahnoon is UAE national security adviser, brother of UAE President, controls G42 (flagged by US intelligence for China military tech links). Subsequently, UAE approved for 500,000 Nvidia AI chips per year, with 1/5 going to G42. Potential quid pro quo under investigation.
